page: Microsoft Azure E16-8ds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V. It features a constrained-core setup that delivers 8 dedicated vCPUs (4 physical cores with 2 threads per core) derived from an Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor clocked at 2.6 GHz. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, the processor includes 35 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, alongside vector instruction support such as AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI. The system offers an abundant 128.0 GB of memory (16.0 GB per vCPU) and bundles 644 GB of local temporary SSD storage without dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark results place the general compute and memory subsystems in the average band across standardized suites. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 8585.83, a Geekbench multi-core score of 4889.0, and a Geekbench single-core score of 1255.0. Memory throughput reaches 49.07 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 36.25 GB/sec for uncached writes, complementing a PassMark memory score of 2495.74 and a Redis SET operational throughput of 7.04 million operations per second. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression yields 27.55 GB/sec, falling into the lower quartile.

Without hardware acceleration, large-scale machine learning execution encounters strict constraints. While lightweight 135M parameter LLM inference handles 173.96 generation tokens per second, scaling to a 7B parameter model reduces generation throughput to 7.32 tokens per second and prompt processing to 14.81 tokens per second. Cost efficiency is optimized for software architectures with per-core licensing fees, where reducing the core footprint from sixteen to eight while retaining the full 128 GB memory allotment yields significant operational savings.

The constrained-core layout makes Microsoft Azure E16-8ds_v4 suitable for memory-intensive workloads that require substantial RAM per vCPU without incurring excess licensing costs. Target use cases include relational database systems, in-memory caching tiers, large analytical data processing, and enterprise enterprise resource planning backends.

The server includes 644 GB of fast local SSD storage and no integrated GPUs. Compute benchmarks demonstrate mid-range capability, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 4889.0, a PassMark CPU score of 8585.83, and Redis throughput of 7.04 million operations per second.
